---
title: "Readiness"
subtitle: "What works now and what remains"
---

MLPerf EDU separates initial usability, quality acceptance, stability, and
production publication. The current milestone focuses on the first two. One
complete authoritative run is enough to evaluate a quality target. Repeated
timing runs remain later work.

## Current Portfolio

All fourteen workloads have a public CLI path, exact target contract, asset
policy, report export, and provenance boundary. Their current quality states
are grouped below.

| **State** | **Workloads** | **Meaning** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Target met | image classification, keyword spotting, anomaly detection, visual wake words, causal language modeling, text classification, information retrieval, graph node classification | At least one complete authoritative `max` result meets the declared target. |
| Target gap recorded | time-series forecasting, code generation, image generation | A complete measurement does not meet the unchanged published reproduction point. |
| Prior target gap; current artifact pending | function calling | The earlier complete audit reached 0.7852 against the unchanged 0.8292 gate. The current runner still needs one complete 1,150-case artifact. |
| Environment-gated | recommendation, reinforcement learning | DLRM and MiniGo require external licensed data, large memory, or a legacy GPU environment. |

The [quality target review](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/QUALITY_TARGET_REVIEW.md)
records the authority and rationale behind every threshold. The
[initial usability checklist](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/READINESS.md)
contains the workload-by-workload results and remaining tasks.
The [independent audit](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md)
records the simulated student, instructor, and benchmark-review verdicts. The
[product readiness plan](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/PRODUCT_READINESS_PLAN.md)
defines the dashboard, assignment, research, and production spirals.

## Assets and Release Policy

Every workload names its exact dataset, split, model source, checkpoint or
training recipe, and evaluator. Some assets are approved for fetch-only use,
while others still require redistribution review. Criteo Terabyte remains a
manual, terms-gated input. These release decisions do not change the benchmark
selection, and the CLI fails closed instead of substituting synthetic data for
an authoritative quality run.

## Normal Student Path

```bash
uv run mlperf doctor
uv run mlperf health
uv run mlperf run --workload image-classification --profile min
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-classification --profile max
uv run mlperf run --workload image-classification --profile max \
  --output-dir submissions/image-classification
```

The final command writes JSON, CSV, HTML, and `.provd.json` files. The HTML
dashboard opens automatically. A `min` report leads with functional readiness,
while a quality-bearing report leads with the metric, target decision, and
normalized target attainment. Both continue with the exact configuration,
hardware, model lineage, and provenance. Use `--no-open-report` on a headless
machine.

The `min` result only confirms setup. A student should use `max` for a graded
quality result when the benchmark's declared environment is available and
preserve the complete artifact set. Every `min` path targets classroom
hardware. DLRM and MiniGo are explicit research-environment exceptions for
their authoritative `max` contracts.

## Research Path

The `pro` profile defaults to the nine-workload research collection. An
individual workload can always be selected, and `--collection all` expands the
plan to all fourteen. Pro runs execute the max contract once by default and
preserve subrun configuration and artifacts in their aggregate result.

```bash
uv run mlperf run --profile pro --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --profile pro --collection all --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --workload information-retrieval --profile pro
```

Optional repetition is available for later stability studies. It is not part
of the current quality-acceptance requirement.

The expected systems behavior is documented for every workload. Measured
working-set, arithmetic-intensity, and dispatch classifications remain later
research-characterization work and are reported as `unmeasured` until trace
evidence exists.

## Production Boundary

The source checkout is suitable for classroom trials and research evaluation.
It is not yet a production package or accepted public benchmark. Component
licensing, package publication, dataset release review, MLCommons governance,
security review, independent hardware reproduction, and authenticated release
artifacts remain open production gates.
